newsitem.title: USA: Russian emigre gets life in U.S. prison for murder.
newsitem.headline: Russian emigre gets life in U.S. prison for murder.

text.p: The estranged wife of prominent Russian scientist Yakov Gluzman was sentenced to life in prison without parole on Wednesday for murdering him with an axe and dismembering his body.

Rita Gluzman was found guilty in January of the April 6, 1996, killing of Gluzman, who was part of a team at Cold Spring Harbour Laboratory on Long Island credited with uncovering a genetic link to cancer in the 1980s.
Gluzman was the first woman to be tried under a federal law that was intended to stop vengeful men from travelling between states to commit domestic violence against women.

The Gluzmans were embroiled in a bitter divorce after a 26-year marriage marked by forced separation, political exile and then professional success after leaving the Soviet Union in the late 1970s for Israel and later the United States.
Prosecutors said Rita Gluzman, 48, killed her 46-year-old husband because he filed for divorce and was planning to start a new life with another woman in Israel.

During January's trial in U.S. District Court in White Plains, New York, Gluzman's cousin Vladimir Zelenin testified against her after pleading guilty to his part in the murder in the hopes of receiving a reduced sentence. He has not been sentenced.
On Wednesday Judge Barrington Parker said the Gluzman affair was "a great tragedy" and that he was imposing the maximum sentence to show "that you have to have respect for the law."
Prosecutors said Gluzman travelled from her $540,000 Upper Saddle River, New Jersey, home to the Pearl River, New York, apartment of her estranged husband, a molecular biologist.
There, she and her cousin ambushed him. According to trial testimony the two cut their victim into more than 67 pieces and dumped the body parts into the Passaic River at East Rutherford, New Jersey.
In court Wednesday, a stoic Gluzman told the judge: "Your honour I did not do it and I want to say it in front of the world, I did not do it."

Gluzman's lawyers argued that she was not involved in the killing and said that Zelenin was solely responsible for the murder. Zelenin testified that they killed the scientist together and that it was his cousin's idea to murder him.
